prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, and for identifying cereblon as the molecular target that explains thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep targeted protein degradation as my single preferred part. It is the one candidate every member ranked, four of us now converge on the identical trio, and the case is mechanistic in the sense I require: a small molecule is made to bring a ubiquitin ligase and a target into one ternary complex, and co-crystal structures show that complex in atomic detail. The three names map onto separable, attributable steps: the heterobifunctional proximity concept and its cellular demonstration (Crews, Deshaies) and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa). The cereblon branch is already clinically established through imid-type drugs, so the part does not rest on the unapproved PROTAC branch alone. I would ask that the citation be written around mechanism, recruitment of a ligase and the molecular explanation of glue action, and not around compound counts or trial status. I do not treat the four-member plurality as a substitute for scientific judgment. It matters to me only because the supporters reached the same trio from different starting points, including Aqvist and Zou, who moved from theory and perovskites on scientific grounds.
statement.case_against: No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so for the PROTAC arm the clinical verdict is pending and the prize could be called early. Handa's cereblon result and the PROTAC concept are two lines of work that a single citation joins by judgment, not by a single discovery. A trio also omits Sakamoto, who co-authored the first PROTAC paper with Crews and Deshaies, and Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made degrader design rational. I cannot settle those priority questions from the material available to me, and the expert reports should be consulted on them before the vote. The chair's question whether a trio that omits Sakamoto is vulnerable is a real one. My answer is that the 2001 paper is a first demonstration with a peptidic ligand that was not generally usable, while the concept's generality was established by the subsequent small-molecule work, so I regard the trio as defensible but not uncontested.

responses.point: Daniel prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B019) with Cullis, Madden and Anderson, as a mature, independently reproduced and clinically validated delivery technology that complements the 2023 Medicine prize, and he lists B056 as his alternative while saying he would weigh clinical maturity.
responses.response: Your pKa-tuned lipid argument is a physical mechanism I respect, and B019 is my first alternative outside the preferred part. Two things keep me from ranking it first. First, the chair's question on the decisive step is unresolved: you name Anderson from the lipidoid screening line, while Sparr names Hope from the Vancouver encapsulation line, so the two supporters of B019 disagree on one of three names. B056 supporters agree on all three. Second, your own case against says the work may be formulation, and I have no expert report that shows which step carries the discovery. On timing, I do not think the lack of an approved PROTAC should defer the prize, because the cereblon branch has years of clinical use. If the experts show that Cullis and Madden carry a decisive, separable step, I would reconsider the order.

responses.point: Emma argues that lipid phase behaviour, non-bilayer structures and controlled mixing explain encapsulation and endosomal release, and that if the decisive step is judged to be lipid-library design her choice would shift toward Anderson.
responses.response: That conditional is honest, and it exposes what bothers me about B019: its attribution depends on a scientific ruling about which step mattered, and the committee has not made that ruling. If Vancouver formulation chemistry decides it, then Hope, MacLachlan, Cullis and Madden compete for three places and MacLachlan's clinical-scale work is left out. If screening decides it, Anderson and Langer enter. In both cases someone with a credible claim is lost, as in B056. The difference is that the three B056 names correspond to different, documented achievements and do not compete for the same one. I also take your point that the 2023 Medicine prize recognised the nucleoside-modification half of the mRNA story, and I do not count it against B019. It is the attribution, not prior recognition, that holds me back.

responses.point: Andrei ranks degradation first and asks whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be one achievement or two parts, and how the three places among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto should be allocated.
responses.response: I considered a two-part configuration, PROTACs for Crews and Deshaies and cereblon glues for Handa and one more name, and I reject it. Induced proximity to a ligase is a single principle that both branches demonstrate, and the molecular explanation of thalidomide is the strongest evidence that the principle is chemically real. Splitting them would also use more of the three-person limit without adding a laureate worth the cost, and it would invite the Ciulli and Gray questions into a second part. I therefore keep one part. Your preference for a mechanism-based citation matches mine, and I have worded the citation so that it rests on ligase recruitment and the cereblon target.

responses.point: Heiner prefers nanopore sensing (B017) with Deamer, Akeson and Bayley, as a transparent physical principle with real adoption, and concedes that the trio excludes Branton and Kasianowicz and that it may be instrumentation more than chemistry.
responses.response: You have stated the weaknesses of B017 more fairly than I did in round 1. The omission of Branton and Kasianowicz, who co-demonstrated translocation in 1996, is the central difficulty, because the reading principle and the engineered pores and motor enzymes are separate contributions that a trio cannot hold together without a priority judgment. I accept your answer on adoption, and I value a principle that can be stated physically. Still, your own concession that the committee may judge this instrumentation and genomics is, for me, enough to keep it below B056. I would take it more seriously if the reports showed that the Bayley and Akeson engineering is a chemical achievement in its own right.

responses.point: Johan moved B056 to first because of breadth of support, still wants the third laureate settled between Handa and Ciulli, and asks that the priority record on the 2001 PROTAC paper and on cereblon be checked before the committee commits.
responses.response: I agree that the priority record should be checked, and I would put it to the expert reports before the vote. On Handa versus Ciulli, I keep Handa. The cereblon identification is a discrete discovery with a clear answer to a decades-old question, and it supports the molecular-glue half of the citation. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are a real design contribution, but they are the stage that follows the proximity concept, and it is in the second tier of the credit problem. I also note that B058 stays outside my preferred part. Car-Parrinello has the cleanest attribution on the list, but I still do not see a case that the field is waiting for it more than for a mechanism-bearing biochemical modality.

responses.point: Xiaodong asks whether the cereblon-directed mechanism is established well enough in structural terms to carry the molecular-glue half of the citation, and says waiting may be wiser if clinical proof is judged insufficient.
responses.response: This is the question I would most like the experts to answer. As I read the record, the structures of cereblon bound to imid drugs, and the ternary complexes with neosubstrates, explain how a small molecule remodels a ligase surface, and that is a physical mechanism of the sort I find convincing. It is established better for the glue branch than for heterobifunctional degraders. I would therefore word the citation so that the cereblon half is carried by the target identification and its structural explanation. On waiting, I do not think perovskites resolve our difficulty: six credited names and unresolved stability questions make the three-person choice harder, not easier.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat degradation as a completed discovery, given that no heterobifunctional degrader is approved.
Whether omitting Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Kim and Ito from a Crews-Deshaies-Handa trio survives a priority review of the 2001 PROTAC paper and of the cereblon identification.
Whether the structural evidence for cereblon-directed degradation is strong enough to carry half of the citation.
Whether B019 can be given a defensible trio once the committee decides between the Vancouver formulation line and the lipidoid screening line.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou. My own research on respiratory-chain proton and electron transfer is adjacent to B004 and B052, which I no longer press, and none of my preferred names or those on the shortlist is tied to me or to Stockholm University on the information available. I see no recusal need. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
